findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with instance or API access.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed improperly.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume, meaning the snapshot data is stored without encryption and could be shared or restored insecurely.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing management access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no other network controls, exposing the web service directly to the internet without any layer of defense such as a load balancer or WAF.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet (including web_host, which also has an open SSH security group) to automatically receive public IPs and be directly reachable from the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing any instance placed in this subnet to automatically receive a public IP address, increasing the internet-facing attack surface.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, allowing network traffic metadata to be stored unencrypted.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is defined to explicitly restrict public access, and force_destroy is enabled, leaving the bucket reliant on default settings which may not adequately prevent public exposure of flow log data.
